cards.note: haben (to have) · present, ich. ich is regular here: the stem hab- plus -e.
haben (to have) · present, du. haben drops the b in the du form: hast, not habst.
haben (to have) · present, er/sie/es. haben drops the b and adds only -t: hat, not habt.
haben (to have) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive, ending in -en.
haben (to have) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t on the stem, and here haben keeps its b.
haben (to have) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. haben is irregular in the Präteritum: hatte with double t, and er ends in -e just like ich.
haben (to have) · perfect, er/sie/es. The participle is regular, ge- + hab + -t, and haben is its own auxiliary.
haben (to have) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem without du; the -e (habe) is optional.
gut (good) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
gut (good) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
gut (good) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: He comes to work in **a good** mood.
cards.back: Er kommt mit **guter** Laune zur Arbeit.
cards.note: gut (good) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
gut (good) · comparative. Comparative adds -er; gut is irregular: besser.
gut (good) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb; gut is irregular: am besten.
sein (to be) · present, ich. sein is completely irregular; ich bin has to be memorised.
sein (to be) · present, du. Irregular stem bi-, but du still ends in -st.
sein (to be) · present, er/sie/es. Irregular: er ist keeps the usual -t ending on an unusual stem.
sein (to be) · present, wir. Irregular: wir and sie (they) both use sind.
sein (to be) · present, ihr. ihr seid is spelled with d; do not confuse it with seit (since).
sein (to be) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Strong Präteritum: the stem becomes war, and er has no ending.
sein (to be) · perfect, er/sie/es. sein builds its perfect with sein itself, and the participle is gewesen.
sein (to be) · imperative, du. The du imperative of sein is irregular: sei.
werden (to become) · present, ich. ich is regular: the stem werd- plus -e.
werden (to become) · present, du. du wirst: e changes to i and the d of the stem drops.
werden (to become) · present, er/sie/es. er wird: e changes to i, and no extra -t because the stem ends in d.
werden (to become) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
werden (to become) · present, ihr. The stem ends in d, so ihr adds -et instead of just -t.
werden (to become) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. The Präteritum switches to u: wurde, and er ends in -e like ich.
werden (to become) · perfect, er/sie/es. werden is a change of state, so the perfect uses sein; the participle is geworden.
werden (to become) · imperative, du. Unlike geben, werden keeps its e in the imperative: werde or werd.
sagen (to say) · present, ich. Regular weak verb: ich takes -e on the stem.
sagen (to say) · present, du. Regular weak verb: du takes -st.
sagen (to say) · present, er/sie/es. Regular weak verb: er takes -t.
sagen (to say) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
sagen (to say) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t, so it looks the same as the er form.
sagen (to say) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Weak Präteritum: stem plus -te, with no vowel change.
sagen (to say) · perfect, er/sie/es. Weak participle: ge- + stem + -t, with haben.
sagen (to say) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem; the -e (sage) is optional.
der Mann (man) · nominative singular. Mann is masculine: der Mann. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Männer, with an umlaut and -er.

cards.front: I see **a man** in front of the house.
cards.back: Ich sehe **einen Mann** vor dem Haus.
cards.note: der Mann (man) · accusative singular. Direct object, so accusative: ein → einen. Only masculine articles change in the accusative; the noun stays the same.
der Mann (man) · dative singular. mit always takes the dative: der → dem. The noun itself takes no ending.
der Mann (man) · genitive singular. Genitive of a masculine noun: des, and the noun adds -es or -s: Mannes.
der Mann (man) · nominative plural. Plural of Mann: umlaut plus -er, Männer. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: The children are playing with **the men**.
cards.note: der Mann (man) · dative plural. mit takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n to the noun: Männer → Männern.
wissen (to know (a fact)) · present, ich. wissen behaves like a modal: ich weiß has no ending.
wissen (to know (a fact)) · present, du. The singular stem is weiß; du adds -t because the ß already gives the s sound.
wissen (to know (a fact)) · present, er/sie/es. Like a modal, er has no ending: er weiß, same as ich.
wissen (to know (a fact)) · present, wir. The plural goes back to the infinitive vowel i: wissen.
wissen (to know (a fact)) · present, ihr. ihr uses the infinitive vowel i and adds -t: wisst.
wissen (to know (a fact)) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Mixed verb: the vowel changes to u and it takes the weak ending -te.
wissen (to know (a fact)) · perfect, er/sie/es. Mixed verb: the participle has ge-, the vowel u and the weak ending -t.
müssen (must, to have to) · present, ich. Modal verb: the singular drops the umlaut and ich has no ending.
müssen (must, to have to) · present, du. Modal verb: no umlaut in the singular, but du still takes -st.
müssen (must, to have to) · present, er/sie/es. Modal verb: er has no ending, so it matches ich muss.
müssen (must, to have to) · present, wir. The plural of a modal keeps the umlaut: müssen.
müssen (must, to have to) · present, ihr. The plural keeps the umlaut, and ihr adds -t: müsst.

cards.front: She **had to** wait a long time.
cards.note: müssen (must, to have to) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. The Präteritum drops the umlaut and adds the weak ending -te.

cards.front: He **had to** go to the doctor.
cards.note: müssen (must, to have to) · perfect, er/sie/es. On its own the participle is gemusst. With another verb the perfect uses the infinitive instead: Er hat gehen müssen.
der Weg (way, path) · nominative singular. Weg is masculine: der Weg. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Wege, with -e.
der Weg (way, path) · accusative singular. Direct object of kennen, so accusative: der → den. The noun stays the same.

cards.front: There is a tree on **the path**.
cards.note: der Weg (way, path) · dative singular. auf for a location takes the dative: der → dem. The noun takes no ending.

cards.front: The end of **the path** is near.
cards.note: der Weg (way, path) · genitive singular. Genitive of a masculine noun: des, and the noun adds -es or -s: Weges.
der Weg (way, path) · nominative plural. Plural of Weg adds -e: Wege. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: We like walking on **the paths** here.
cards.back: Wir laufen gern auf **den Wegen** hier.
cards.note: der Weg (way, path) · dative plural. auf for a location takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n: Wege → Wegen.
einfach (easy, simple) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
einfach (easy, simple) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
einfach (easy, simple) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.
einfach (easy, simple) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
einfach (easy, simple) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: einfacher.
einfach (easy, simple) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb.
leben (to live) · present, ich. Regular weak verb: ich takes -e.
leben (to live) · present, du. Regular weak verb: du takes -st.
leben (to live) · present, er/sie/es. Regular weak verb: er takes -t.
leben (to live) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
leben (to live) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t, the same as the er form.

cards.front: He **lived** in Italy for a long time.
cards.note: leben (to live) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Weak Präteritum: stem plus -te.

cards.front: She **lived** in Paris for two years.
cards.note: leben (to live) · perfect, er/sie/es. Weak participle: ge- + stem + -t, with haben.
leben (to live) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem; leb wohl is a fixed goodbye.
kommen (to come) · present, ich. kommen is regular in the present: ich takes -e.
kommen (to come) · present, du. No vowel change in the present: du simply takes -st.
kommen (to come) · present, er/sie/es. No vowel change in the present: er simply takes -t.
kommen (to come) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
kommen (to come) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t on the stem.
kommen (to come) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Strong Präteritum: o changes to a, and er has no ending.
kommen (to come) · perfect, er/sie/es. kommen is a verb of motion, so the perfect uses sein, not haben.
kommen (to come) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem, usually without -e.
wollen (to want) · present, ich. Modal verb: the singular changes o to i, and ich has no ending.
wollen (to want) · present, du. Modal verb: singular stem will-, and du takes -st.
wollen (to want) · present, er/sie/es. Modal verb: er has no ending, so it matches ich will.
wollen (to want) · present, wir. The plural goes back to the infinitive vowel o.
wollen (to want) · present, ihr. The plural keeps the o, and ihr adds -t.
wollen (to want) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Modals take the weak Präteritum ending -te: wollte.
wollen (to want) · perfect, er/sie/es. On its own the participle is gewollt. With another verb the perfect uses the infinitive instead: Sie hat kommen wollen.
die Frau (woman) · nominative singular. Frau is feminine: die Frau. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Frauen, with -en.

cards.front: I know **the woman** from the shop.
cards.back: Ich kenne **die Frau** aus dem Laden.
cards.note: die Frau (woman) · accusative singular. Direct object, so accusative. Feminine articles do not change in the accusative: die stays die.
die Frau (woman) · dative singular. geben puts the receiver in the dative: die → der. Feminine nouns never take an ending in the singular.
die Frau (woman) · genitive singular. Genitive of a feminine noun: die → der, and the noun takes no ending.
die Frau (woman) · nominative plural. Plural of Frau adds -en: Frauen. All plurals take die in the nominative.
die Frau (woman) · dative plural. mit takes the dative: plural article den. Frauen already ends in -n, so nothing is added.
lassen (to let, to leave) · present, ich. ich is regular: no vowel change, just -e.
lassen (to let, to leave) · present, du. a changes to ä in the du form, and -st shrinks to -t after the ss.
lassen (to let, to leave) · present, er/sie/es. a changes to ä in the er form, so it looks the same as du lässt.
lassen (to let, to leave) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
lassen (to let, to leave) · present, ihr. No umlaut in the ihr form; the -t joins the stem: lasst.

cards.front: She **left** her bag in the car.
cards.note: lassen (to let, to leave) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Strong Präteritum: a changes to ie, ss becomes ß, and er has no ending.
lassen (to let, to leave) · perfect, er/sie/es. Strong participle: ge- + stem + -en, with no vowel change.
lassen (to let, to leave) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem and has no umlaut.
klar (clear) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.

cards.front: In the morning I have **a clear** head.
cards.back: Am Morgen habe ich **einen klaren** Kopf.
cards.note: klar (clear) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
klar (clear) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: In **clear** visibility you can see the mountains.
cards.back: Bei **klarer** Sicht sieht man die Berge.
cards.note: klar (clear) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
klar (clear) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: klarer.

cards.back: Im Winter ist die Luft **am klarsten**.
cards.note: klar (clear) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb.
der Vater (father) · nominative singular. Vater is masculine: der Vater. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Väter, with only an umlaut.

cards.front: The child is looking for **the father**.
cards.note: der Vater (father) · accusative singular. Direct object of suchen, so accusative: der → den. The noun stays the same.

cards.front: I am helping **the father** with the car.
cards.back: Ich helfe **dem Vater** mit dem Auto.
cards.note: der Vater (father) · dative singular. helfen takes the dative: der → dem. The noun takes no ending.
der Vater (father) · genitive singular. Genitive of a masculine noun: des, and the noun adds -s: Vaters.

cards.front: **The fathers** are waiting at the school.
cards.note: der Vater (father) · nominative plural. Plural of Vater only adds an umlaut: Väter. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: The teacher is talking to **the fathers**.
cards.note: der Vater (father) · dative plural. mit takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n: Väter → Vätern.
der Tag (day) · nominative singular. Tag is masculine: der Tag. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Tage, with -e.
der Tag (day) · accusative singular. Direct object of brauchen, so accusative: ein → einen. The noun stays the same.

cards.front: He works ten hours in **one day**.
cards.back: Er arbeitet an **einem Tag** zehn Stunden.
cards.note: der Tag (day) · dative singular. an with a point in time takes the dative: ein → einem. The noun takes no ending.

cards.front: The end of **the day** is quiet.
cards.note: der Tag (day) · genitive singular. Genitive of a masculine noun: des, and the noun adds -es or -s: Tages.
der Tag (day) · nominative plural. Plural of Tag adds -e: Tage. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: I am coming back in three **days**.
cards.note: der Tag (day) · dative plural. in with a period of time takes the dative; dative plural adds -n to the noun: Tage → Tagen.
die Mutter (mother) · nominative singular. Mutter is feminine: die Mutter. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Mütter, with only an umlaut.
die Mutter (mother) · accusative singular. Direct object of fragen, so accusative. Feminine articles do not change: die stays die.

cards.front: The child helps **the mother** in the kitchen.
cards.back: Das Kind hilft **der Mutter** in der Küche.
cards.note: die Mutter (mother) · dative singular. helfen takes the dative: die → der. Feminine nouns take no ending in the singular.

cards.front: **The mother's** phone is on the table.
cards.back: Das Handy **der Mutter** liegt auf dem Tisch.
cards.note: die Mutter (mother) · genitive singular. Genitive of a feminine noun: die → der, and the noun takes no ending.

cards.front: **The mothers** are sitting on the bench.
cards.note: die Mutter (mother) · nominative plural. Plural of Mutter only adds an umlaut: Mütter. All plurals take die in the nominative.
die Mutter (mother) · dative plural. zu always takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n: Mütter → Müttern.
helfen (to help) · present, ich. No vowel change for ich: the stem helf- plus -e.
helfen (to help) · present, du. helfen changes e to i in the du and er forms: hilfst.
helfen (to help) · present, er/sie/es. helfen changes e to i in the er form, plus -t: hilft.
helfen (to help) · present, wir. The plural has no vowel change: helfen.
helfen (to help) · present, ihr. The e to i change only affects du and er, so ihr keeps the e: helft.
helfen (to help) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Strong Präteritum: e changes to a, and er has no ending.
helfen (to help) · perfect, er/sie/es. Strong participle with a vowel change to o: geholfen.
helfen (to help) · imperative, du. The du imperative drops -st and the pronoun; e to i verbs keep the i.
die Nacht (night) · nominative singular. Nacht is feminine: die Nacht. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Nächte, with an umlaut and -e.

cards.front: I am staying **one night** in Berlin.
cards.note: die Nacht (night) · accusative singular. A length of time without a preposition is accusative. Feminine eine does not change.
die Nacht (night) · dative singular. in for a time takes the dative: die → der. Feminine nouns take no ending.

cards.front: The quiet of **the night** is lovely.
cards.note: die Nacht (night) · genitive singular. Genitive of a feminine noun: die → der, and the noun takes no ending.
die Nacht (night) · nominative plural. Plural of Nacht: umlaut plus -e, Nächte. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.back: Nach drei **Nächten** fahren wir nach Hause.
cards.note: die Nacht (night) · dative plural. nach always takes the dative; dative plural adds -n to the noun: Nächte → Nächten.
finden (to find) · present, ich. Regular in the present: ich takes -e.
finden (to find) · present, du. The stem ends in d, so an e is added before the ending: findest.
finden (to find) · present, er/sie/es. The stem ends in d, so an e is added before -t: findet.
finden (to find) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.

cards.front: **Can** you **find** the way on your own?
cards.note: finden (to find) · present, ihr. After a d stem, ihr also adds -et: findet.

cards.front: She **found** a wallet on the street.
cards.back: Sie **fand** eine Geldbörse auf der Straße.
cards.note: finden (to find) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Strong Präteritum: i changes to a, and er has no ending.
finden (to find) · perfect, er/sie/es. Strong participle with a vowel change to u: gefunden.
finden (to find) · imperative, du. Stems ending in d usually keep the -e in the imperative: finde.
geben (to give) · present, ich. No vowel change for ich: the stem geb- plus -e.
geben (to give) · present, du. geben changes e to i in the du and er forms: gibst.
geben (to give) · present, er/sie/es. geben changes e to i in the er form, plus -t: gibt.

cards.front: We **are throwing** a party on Saturday.
cards.note: geben (to give) · present, wir. The plural has no vowel change: geben.
geben (to give) · present, ihr. The e to i change only affects du and er, so ihr keeps the e: gebt.
geben (to give) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Strong Präteritum: e changes to a, and er has no ending.
geben (to give) · perfect, er/sie/es. Strong participle: ge- + stem + -en, keeping the e: gegeben.
geben (to give) · imperative, du. The du imperative drops -st and the pronoun; e to i verbs keep the i.
hören (to hear, to listen) · present, ich. Regular weak verb: ich takes -e.
hören (to hear, to listen) · present, du. Regular weak verb: du takes -st.
hören (to hear, to listen) · present, er/sie/es. Regular weak verb: er takes -t.
hören (to hear, to listen) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
hören (to hear, to listen) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t, the same as the er form.
hören (to hear, to listen) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Weak Präteritum: stem plus -te.
hören (to hear, to listen) · perfect, er/sie/es. Weak participle: ge- + stem + -t, with haben.
hören (to hear, to listen) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem; zu goes to the end because zuhören is separable.
das Mädchen (girl) · nominative singular. Mädchen is neuter, like every noun in -chen: das Mädchen. The plural is the same word, die Mädchen.

cards.front: I see **a girl** with a dog.
cards.back: Ich sehe **ein Mädchen** mit einem Hund.
cards.note: das Mädchen (girl) · accusative singular. Direct object, so accusative. Neuter ein does not change in the accusative.

cards.front: The teacher gives **the girl** a book.
cards.back: Der Lehrer gibt **dem Mädchen** ein Buch.
cards.note: das Mädchen (girl) · dative singular. geben puts the receiver in the dative: das → dem. The noun takes no ending.
das Mädchen (girl) · genitive singular. Genitive of a neuter noun: des, and the noun adds -s: Mädchens.
das Mädchen (girl) · nominative plural. The plural of Mädchen is the same word; only the article shows it: das → die.
das Mädchen (girl) · dative plural. mit takes the dative: plural article den. Mädchen already ends in -n, so nothing is added.
der Abend (evening) · nominative singular. Abend is masculine: der Abend. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Abende, with -e.

cards.front: We are spending **an evening** in town.
cards.back: Wir verbringen **einen Abend** in der Stadt.
cards.note: der Abend (evening) · accusative singular. Direct object of verbringen, so accusative: ein → einen. The noun stays the same.

cards.front: I'll tell you about **an evening** in Paris.
cards.back: Ich erzähle dir von **einem Abend** in Paris.
cards.note: der Abend (evening) · dative singular. von always takes the dative: ein → einem. The noun takes no ending.

cards.front: The music of **the evening** was great.
cards.note: der Abend (evening) · genitive singular. Genitive of a masculine noun: des, and the noun adds -s: Abends.
der Abend (evening) · nominative plural. Plural of Abend adds -e: Abende. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: In **the evenings** I like to read.
cards.note: der Abend (evening) · dative plural. an with a time takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n: Abende → Abenden.
das Haus (house) · nominative singular. Haus is neuter: das Haus. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Häuser, with an umlaut and -er.
das Haus (house) · accusative singular. Direct object of kaufen, so accusative. Neuter ein does not change in the accusative.

cards.front: A car is parked in front of **the house**.
cards.note: das Haus (house) · dative singular. vor for a place takes the dative: das → dem. The noun takes no ending.

cards.front: The door of **the house** is blue.
cards.note: das Haus (house) · genitive singular. Genitive of a neuter noun: des, and the noun adds -es: Hauses.
das Haus (house) · nominative plural. Plural of Haus: umlaut plus -er, Häuser. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: There is a park between **the houses**.
cards.note: das Haus (house) · dative plural. zwischen for a place takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n: Häuser → Häusern.
der Freund (friend) · nominative singular. Freund is masculine: der Freund, ein Freund. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Freunde, with -e.

cards.front: I am visiting **a friend** in Hamburg.

cards.front: I am writing **a friend** an email.

der Freund (friend) · genitive singular. Genitive of a masculine noun: des, and the noun adds -es or -s: Freundes.
der Freund (friend) · nominative plural. Plural of Freund adds -e: Freunde. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: I am going to Italy with **friends**.
cards.note: der Freund (friend) · dative plural. mit takes the dative; dative plural adds -n to the noun: Freunde → Freunden.
essen (to eat) · present, ich. No vowel change for ich: the stem ess- plus -e.
essen (to eat) · present, du. essen changes e to i in the du form, and -st shrinks to -t after the ss.
essen (to eat) · present, er/sie/es. essen changes e to i in the er form, so it looks the same as du isst.
essen (to eat) · present, wir. The plural has no vowel change: essen.
essen (to eat) · present, ihr. ihr keeps the e and adds -t: esst.
essen (to eat) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Strong Präteritum: e changes to a, ss becomes ß, and er has no ending.
essen (to eat) · perfect, er/sie/es. The participle gegessen has an extra g between ge- and the stem.
essen (to eat) · imperative, du. The du imperative drops -st and the pronoun; e to i verbs keep the i.
die Welt (world) · nominative singular. Welt is feminine: die Welt. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Welten, with -en.
die Welt (world) · accusative singular. Direct object of sehen, so accusative. Feminine articles do not change: die stays die.

cards.note: die Welt (world) · nominative plural. Plural of Welt adds -en: Welten. All plurals take die in the nominative.
die Welt (world) · dative plural. von takes the dative. Welten already ends in -n, so nothing is added.
schnell (fast) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
schnell (fast) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
schnell (fast) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: With **fast** delivery the parcel arrives tomorrow.
cards.back: Mit **schneller** Lieferung kommt das Paket morgen.
cards.note: schnell (fast) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.

cards.front: The train is **faster** than the bus.
cards.back: Der Zug ist **schneller** als der Bus.
cards.note: schnell (fast) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: schneller.
schnell (fast) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb.
nehmen (to take) · present, ich. No vowel change for ich: the stem nehm- plus -e.
nehmen (to take) · present, du. nehmen changes eh to imm in the du and er forms: nimmst.
nehmen (to take) · present, er/sie/es. nehmen changes eh to imm in the er form, plus -t: nimmt.
nehmen (to take) · present, wir. The plural has no vowel change: nehmen.
nehmen (to take) · present, ihr. The vowel change only affects du and er, so ihr keeps the e: nehmt.
nehmen (to take) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Strong Präteritum: e changes to a, and er has no ending.
nehmen (to take) · perfect, er/sie/es. Strong participle with a vowel change to o and a double m: genommen.
nehmen (to take) · imperative, du. The du imperative drops -st and the pronoun; e to i verbs keep the i: nimm.
glauben (to believe) · present, ich. Regular weak verb: ich takes -e.
glauben (to believe) · present, du. Regular weak verb: du takes -st.
glauben (to believe) · present, er/sie/es. Regular weak verb: er takes -t.
glauben (to believe) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
glauben (to believe) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t, the same as the er form.
glauben (to believe) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Weak Präteritum: stem plus -te.
glauben (to believe) · perfect, er/sie/es. Weak participle: ge- + stem + -t, with haben.
glauben (to believe) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem; the -e (glaube) is optional.
bringen (to bring) · present, ich. Regular in the present: ich takes -e.

cards.front: **Will** you **bring** me a glass of water?
cards.note: bringen (to bring) · present, du. No vowel change in the present: du takes -st.
bringen (to bring) · present, er/sie/es. No vowel change in the present: er takes -t.

cards.front: We **are taking** the children to school.
cards.note: bringen (to bring) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
bringen (to bring) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t, the same as the er form.
bringen (to bring) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Mixed verb: the stem changes to brach- and takes the weak ending -te.
bringen (to bring) · perfect, er/sie/es. Mixed verb: changed stem brach- with the weak participle ending -t: gebracht.
bringen (to bring) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem; the -e (bringe) is optional.
brauchen (to need) · present, ich. Regular weak verb: ich takes -e.
brauchen (to need) · present, du. Regular weak verb: du takes -st.

cards.front: The baby **needs** a lot of sleep.
cards.note: brauchen (to need) · present, er/sie/es. Regular weak verb: er takes -t.
brauchen (to need) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
brauchen (to need) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t, the same as the er form.
brauchen (to need) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Weak Präteritum: stem plus -te, no umlaut in standard German.
brauchen (to need) · perfect, er/sie/es. Weak participle: ge- + stem + -t, with haben.
brauchen (to need) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem; the -e (brauche) is optional.
der Junge (boy) · nominative singular. Junge is masculine: der Junge. It is a weak noun: -n in every form except this one, so the plural is Jungen.
der Junge (boy) · accusative singular. Direct object, so accusative: der → den. Junge is a weak noun, so it adds -n: Jungen.

cards.front: The mother gives **the boy** an apple.
cards.back: Die Mutter gibt **dem Jungen** einen Apfel.
cards.note: der Junge (boy) · dative singular. geben puts the receiver in the dative: der → dem. As a weak noun, Junge adds -n.
der Junge (boy) · genitive singular. Genitive: des. Junge is a weak noun, so it adds -n, not -s: Jungen.
der Junge (boy) · nominative plural. Plural of the weak noun Junge adds -n: Jungen. All plurals take die in the nominative.
der Junge (boy) · dative plural. mit takes the dative: plural article den. Jungen already ends in -n, so nothing is added.
fragen (to ask) · present, ich. Regular weak verb: ich takes -e.
fragen (to ask) · present, du. Regular weak verb: du takes -st, with no umlaut.
fragen (to ask) · present, er/sie/es. Regular weak verb: er takes -t, with no umlaut.
fragen (to ask) · present, wir. wir uses the same form as the infinitive.
fragen (to ask) · present, ihr. ihr takes -t, the same as the er form.
fragen (to ask) · simple past (Präteritum), er/sie/es. Weak Präteritum: stem plus -te, not a strong form.
fragen (to ask) · perfect, er/sie/es. Weak participle: ge- + stem + -t, with haben.
fragen (to ask) · imperative, du. The du imperative is the bare stem; the -e (frage) is optional.
die Familie (family) · nominative singular. Familie is feminine: die Familie. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Familien, with -n.
die Familie (family) · accusative singular. Direct object of besuchen, so accusative. Feminine articles do not change: die stays die.

cards.front: He lives with **a family** in Spain.
cards.back: Er wohnt bei **einer Familie** in Spanien.
cards.note: die Familie (family) · dative singular. bei always takes the dative: eine → einer. Feminine nouns take no ending.
die Familie (family) · genitive singular. Genitive of a feminine noun: die → der, and the noun takes no ending.
die Familie (family) · nominative plural. Plural of Familie adds -n: Familien. All plurals take die in the nominative.
die Familie (family) · dative plural. helfen takes the dative: plural article den. Familien already ends in -n, so nothing is added.
das Problem (problem) · nominative singular. Problem is neuter: das Problem. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Probleme, with -e.
das Problem (problem) · accusative singular. Direct object of haben, so accusative. Neuter ein does not change in the accusative.

cards.front: Can you help me with **the problem**?
cards.back: Kannst du mir mit **dem Problem** helfen?
cards.note: das Problem (problem) · dative singular. mit always takes the dative: das → dem. The noun takes no ending.

cards.front: The solution to **the problem** is simple.
cards.note: das Problem (problem) · genitive singular. Genitive of a neuter noun: des, and the noun adds -s: Problems.
das Problem (problem) · nominative plural. Plural of Problem adds -e: Probleme. All plurals take die in the nominative.
das Problem (problem) · dative plural. mit takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n: Probleme → Problemen.
der Sohn (son) · nominative singular. Sohn is masculine: der Sohn. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Söhne, with an umlaut and -e.
der Sohn (son) · accusative singular. Direct object of haben, so accusative: ein → einen. The noun stays the same.
der Sohn (son) · dative singular. geben puts the receiver in the dative: der → dem. The noun takes no ending.
der Sohn (son) · genitive singular. Genitive of a masculine noun: des, and the noun adds -es or -s: Sohnes.
der Sohn (son) · nominative plural. Plural of Sohn: umlaut plus -e, Söhne. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: She lives with **the sons** in Cologne.
cards.back: Sie wohnt mit **den Söhnen** in Köln.
cards.note: der Sohn (son) · dative plural. mit takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n: Söhne → Söhnen.
die Frage (question) · nominative singular. Frage is feminine: die Frage. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Fragen, with -n.
die Frage (question) · accusative singular. Direct object of haben, so accusative. Feminine eine does not change.
die Frage (question) · dative singular. bei always takes the dative: die → der. Feminine nouns take no ending.

cards.front: The point of **the question** is unclear.
cards.note: die Frage (question) · genitive singular. Genitive of a feminine noun: die → der, and the noun takes no ending.
die Frage (question) · nominative plural. Plural of Frage adds -n: Fragen. All plurals take die in the nominative.

cards.front: After **the questions** we take a break.
cards.back: Nach **den Fragen** machen wir eine Pause.
cards.note: die Frage (question) · dative plural. nach always takes the dative: plural article den. Fragen already ends in -n, so nothing is added.
der Kopf (head) · nominative singular. Kopf is masculine: der Kopf. Subject, so nominative; the plural is Köpfe, with an umlaut and -e.
der Kopf (head) · accusative singular. Direct object of schütteln, so accusative: der → den. German uses the article for body parts.

cards.front: She is wearing a hat on **her head**.
cards.back: Sie trägt eine Mütze auf **dem Kopf**.
cards.note: der Kopf (head) · dative singular. auf for a place takes the dative: der → dem. The noun takes no ending.

cards.front: The size of **the head** matters for the helmet.
cards.back: Die Größe **des Kopfes** ist wichtig für den Helm.
cards.note: der Kopf (head) · genitive singular. Genitive of a masculine noun: des, and the noun adds -es or -s: Kopfes.
der Kopf (head) · nominative plural. Plural of Kopf: umlaut plus -e, Köpfe. Here it stands without an article, after alle.
der Kopf (head) · dative plural. mit takes the dative; dative plural uses den and adds -n: Köpfe → Köpfen.
toll (great) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
toll (great) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
toll (great) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: We dance all night to **great** music.
cards.back: Bei **toller** Musik tanzen wir die ganze Nacht.
cards.note: toll (great) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
toll (great) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: toller.

cards.front: The holiday by the sea was **the greatest**.
cards.back: Der Urlaub am Meer war **am tollsten**.
cards.note: toll (great) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb.

cards.front: **The long** way to school is tiring.
cards.back: **Der weite** Weg zur Schule ist anstrengend.
cards.note: weit (far, wide) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
weit (far, wide) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.

cards.front: **A loose** dress is comfortable in summer.
cards.back: **Ein weites** Kleid ist im Sommer bequem.
cards.note: weit (far, wide) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: You can see the sea in the **far** distance.
cards.back: In **weiter** Ferne sieht man das Meer.
cards.note: weit (far, wide) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
weit (far, wide) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: weiter.
weit (far, wide) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb; after -t an extra e is added: -esten.

cards.front: **The quiet** park is behind the house.
cards.back: **Der ruhige** Park liegt hinter dem Haus.
cards.note: ruhig (quiet, calm) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.

cards.front: We are looking for **a quiet** spot.
cards.note: ruhig (quiet, calm) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
ruhig (quiet, calm) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: She explains everything in **a calm** voice.
cards.note: ruhig (quiet, calm) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
ruhig (quiet, calm) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: ruhiger.

cards.back: Am Sonntag ist die Stadt **am ruhigsten**.
cards.note: ruhig (quiet, calm) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb.
nett (nice) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
nett (nice) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
nett (nice) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.back: In **netter** Gesellschaft vergeht die Zeit schnell.
cards.note: nett (nice) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
nett (nice) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: netter.
nett (nice) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb; after -t an extra e is added: -esten.

cards.front: **The important** appointment is tomorrow at nine.
cards.back: **Der wichtige** Termin ist morgen um neun.
cards.note: wichtig (important) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
wichtig (important) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
wichtig (important) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: I'll call you if there is **important** mail.
cards.back: Bei **wichtiger** Post rufe ich dich an.
cards.note: wichtig (important) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
wichtig (important) · comparative. Comparative adds -er; German never uses mehr for this.
wichtig (important) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb.
schlecht (bad) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
schlecht (bad) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
schlecht (bad) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.back: Bei **schlechter** Luft kann ich nicht schlafen.
cards.note: schlecht (bad) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
schlecht (bad) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: schlechter.
schlecht (bad) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb; after -t an extra e is added: -esten.

cards.front: **The free** seat is next to me.
cards.note: frei (free) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
frei (free) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
frei (free) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: Children love playing out in the **open** countryside.
cards.note: frei (free) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er. "in freier Natur" is a fixed phrase.

cards.back: Nach der Prüfung fühle ich mich **freier**.
cards.note: frei (free) · comparative. Comparative adds -er to the adjective: freier.

cards.back: Am Meer fühle ich mich **am freiesten**.
cards.note: frei (free) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb; after a vowel an extra e is common: -esten.
schwierig (difficult) · after der, masculine nominative. After der the article already shows the case, so the adjective takes the weak ending -e.
schwierig (difficult) · after ein, masculine accusative. After einen the adjective takes -en: masculine accusative.
schwierig (difficult) · after ein, neuter nominative. ein does not show neuter, so the adjective does: -es.

cards.front: I often take breaks during **difficult** work.
cards.back: Bei **schwieriger** Arbeit mache ich oft Pausen.
cards.note: schwierig (difficult) · no article, feminine dative. With no article the adjective carries the case ending itself: feminine dative -er.
schwierig (difficult) · comparative. Comparative adds -er; German never uses mehr for this.
schwierig (difficult) · superlative. am + -sten is the superlative used after a verb.
